maya: hi all, i'm maya (started last monday). trying to compile the runtime on Ubuntu 22.04 bare-metal (RTX A5000). followed the build doc but hit linker errors around cudnn. any pointers? :wave:

joe: welcome! paste the exact error and `ls /usr/local/cuda` + `dpkg -l | grep cudnn`

maya: thanks. main errors during make are:

```
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcudnn_static
/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcudnn
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
...
/usr/local/cuda/include/cudnn.h:49:10: fatal error: cudnn_version.h: No such file or directory
 #include <cudnn_version.h>
          ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```

ls shows CUDA 12.1 installed at /usr/local/cuda-12.1 and /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-12.1
`dpkg -l | grep cudnn` returns nothing (i didn't install cuDNN manually)

ryan: looks like cuDNN dev libs/headers are missing. we don't package cudnn in the repo due to licensing. install the cudnn dev package from NVIDIA (deb) or manually drop the headers/libs into /usr/local/cuda/include and lib64. For Ubuntu: download libcudnn8_8.*.deb and libcudnn8-dev_8.*.deb matching your CUDA version.

joe: extra notes: 1) make sure libcuda.so (driver) is visible at link time — that's separate from libcudnn. 2) if you installed cuDNN tarball, ensure `sudo cp include/cudnn*.h /usr/local/cuda/include` and `sudo cp lib/libcudnn* /usr/local/cuda/lib64` then `sudo ldconfig`

maya: i tried copying headers from the cudnn tarball into /usr/local/cuda/include but still get `/usr/bin/ld: cannot find -lcudnn_static`. lib64 only has libcudnn.so, not libcudnn_static.a. build expects shared lib, though.

ryan: you can either install the -dev .deb (recommended) which provides the symlinks, or create the missing static lib by `ar rcs libcudnn_static.a libcuda.a` (not recommended). also check the cmake output: it might pick up an old pkgconfig. run `cmake .. -DCUDNN_ROOT=/usr/local/cuda-12.1 -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` to force it.

devex: for onboarding, update: add step to DevEx doc to state "Install cuDNN runtime + dev libs matching CUDA version" and include links to the correct download page + note about accepting Nvidia EULA. filing a quick PR after this thread.

maya: another puzzler: after installing libcudnn8-dev, cmake finds cudnn but later nvcc complains: `error: host compiler gcc version is incompatible` showing gcc 13 on my machine. our doc says gcc-11/12. what to do?

joe: nvcc often requires a supported host compiler. either install gcc-11/g++-11 and point cmake at them or use the dev-container image which has matching toolchain. e.g. `sudo apt install gcc-11 g++-11` then `cmake .. -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/usr/bin/gcc-11 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++-11`

ryan: if you don't want to change system default, use `update-alternatives` to create entries and switch for the build, or docker container to avoid messing with host toolchain. Also check the nvcc `--compiler-bindir` option if you want to pass a different gcc directly to nvcc.

maya: ok installed libcudnn8-dev and installed gcc-11. reran cmake and now build fails later with `undefined reference to __cudaRegisterHostFunction` during linking. looks like missing -lcudart or wrong link order?

joe: that symbol's from cuda runtime. ensure link includes -lcudart_static or -lcudart and that /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 has libcudart.so. Also verify `ldd` on the failing object to see unresolved symbols. If you used static cudnn and dynamic cudart, link order matters. Try adding `-Wl,--start-group -lcudart -lcudnn -Wl,--end-group` in the linking flags (CMake: target_link_libraries with INTERFACE link options) as a quick test.

ryan: one more gotcha: if you installed cuda via package manager and also have distro packages (e.g. `nvidia-cuda-toolkit`), they can conflict. `which nvcc` and `nvcc --version` should point to /usr/local/cuda-12.1/bin/nvcc. If not, update PATH.

infra-bot: infra note: if you want a preconfigured environment, request a gpu-dev VM (ttl 48h) with CUDA 12.1 + cuDNN 8.4 + gcc-11. Opened ticket DEVVM-589 for maya per request.

maya: thanks everyone. i switched to the dev VM from infra (quick start, much appreciated). ran inside the VM, build succeeded after applying the -DCUDNN_ROOT and using gcc-11. will follow up with the devex PR to add cuDNN step. closing loop here. :tada:

devex: PR raised: devex/docs#412 "onboarding: explicit cuDNN install step for GPU builds" — tagging onboarding and eng-runtime.

joe: great! we'll add a short note about static vs shared cuDNN and nvcc compiler versions. welcome aboard again :clap:
